title: Chapter 3. The Account of the Manifestation of Virachandra's Line
html:
The brahmana Sudhamaya of Mahesh and Narayani, daughter of the Ocean; Nityananda's departure and Virachandra's anointing; initiation from Jahnava; the journey to Nilachala and the wedding; the subduing of the Nadas; Virachandra's sons and daughter (pp. 30–40)

[p. 30]

1Sri Virachandra — the moon that dispels the darkness of the Kali age;
the moon that makes the night-lotuses of his devotees bloom;
the moon shining in the night for the eyes of Sri Jahnava and others;
the full moon in distributing the nectar of prema1.

2Glory, glory to Nityananda, glory to the Merciful One,
by merely uttering whose name bhakti becomes perfect.

3In Mahesh there lived a brahmana of pure heart;
the worship of Vishnu and the Vaishnavas was his daily duty.

4His name was Sudhamaya; he was the son-in-law of Pipilai2,
and his wife was named Vidyunmala.

5Devoted to Vishnu, pure, faithful to her husband,
she always stood by her husband with joined palms.

[p. 31]

6"I have neither daughter nor son — my life passes in vain.
What joy is there in staying in worldly life, and for the sake of what attachment?"

7The Mukhuti3 replied: "Faithful wife, my mind is the same:
I have been bound to the house — I tell you the truth.

8With the pilgrims going to the Lord's Chandana-yatra4
let us go too, to see Sri Mukunda.

9It is by his mercy that this has arisen in your heart.
Come, let us go and see Jagannatha."

10Saying this, the best of brahmanas called out the name of Hari,
and Sudhamaya floated in an ocean of bliss.

11On the fifth day he invited the brahmanas of his village
and fed them with the four kinds of food5.

12All the goods that were in the house he gave away to the brahmanas,
and honored each of them with garlands and fragrances.

13At that time all the pilgrims arrived,
and at a great festival they were fed.

14Rising at dawn, the best of brahmanas, taking his wife along,
set out with the Vaishnavas, delighting in talk of Hari.

15The rest of his property — whatever money and jewels remained —
he took with him for the offering of food to Jagannatha.

16Step by step they came to Nilachala;
calling "Hari, Hari!" they felt no weariness on the road.

17Seeing the Lord's beautiful face, he felt his life fulfilled,
and he went round all the holy places.

18He took great joy in the festival of the chariots,
and whatever he had saved he spent on the festivities.

19Staying there for the chaturmasya6 and visiting the holy places,
he said these words to his wife:

20"Let us go to a solitary place on the shore of the ocean
and perform sadhana to attain the Best of the Yadus."

21Going there, they made a small hut of leaves,
and both of them chanted the name of Murari without cease.

22After a long time, pleased with their meditation, the Ocean
came to them, bringing a girl with him.

23Taking on a visible form, the kindly Ocean
set the girl before the brahmana and gently said:

24"Take this girl and raise her with care;
through her you will gain the jewel among men.

25Through this girl your family will be delivered;
through this girl you will cross the ocean of worldly life.

26This girl, named Narayani, is Lakshmi herself;
Ganga entrusted her to me, and I give her to you out of mercy.

27No groom in the three worlds is worthy of her:
the Lord's energy is fit only for the Lord."

28The brahmana said: "I am a very poor brahmana.
How will Lakshmi be raised by me?"

29The Ocean said: "Brahmana, do not fear.
This is no bad dream — it is the truth7.

30She will live with you visibly, won over by your affection,
and will think of her Lord without cease.

31He is Gauranga himself, Vishnu, the abode of the universe;
he is Nityananda's son8, and his name is Sri Virachandra.

32Soon, while visiting holy places, he will come here,
take this girl as his wife and make you blessed."

33Saying this, the Ocean vanished,
and the brahmana and his wife were filled with joy.

[p. 32]

34"When will Virachandra Prabhu grant us his sight?" —
day and night this was the worship of the two of them.

35Now hear the account of Nityananda,
by hearing which one attains Gaura, the Lord.

36Glory, glory to Nityananda, glory to the Merciful One,
by whose mercy perfection in bhakti-yoga and knowledge is attained.

37Remembering his name destroys the bonds of worldly life;
whoever takes his name becomes a servant of Gauranga.

38The best of all avataras is Chaitanya Gosai,
and his second body is the brother Nityananda.

39In separation from Chaitanya, Prabhu wept constantly;
when he occasionally returned to outer awareness, he spoke of Chaitanya.

40With body, mind and speech he always meditated on Chaitanya
and sang Gauranga's virtues in a loud voice.

41He himself sang of Gauranga and made the whole world sing:
"Sing the virtues of Gauranga and you will attain the son of Nanda!"

42He himself chanted Gauranga's name in his heart;
apart from devotion to Gaura, Nitai knew nothing.

43He lived constantly at Khardaha, in his inner rooms,
and Sri Vasu and Jahnava ever increased their love for him9.

44Overwhelmed with love for Gaura, he did not know day from night,
and at times he saw Gaura's radiance even in Shyamasundara.

45Who can understand Nityananda's power?
Entering the temple, he vanished from sight.

46Then Prabhu, reflecting in his mind, came back to himself,
and taking Vasu and Jahnava with him, set out.

47From there he went to Ekachakra
and beheld Bankimdeva there.

48For some days he gazed upon Bankimdeva there,
and then he disappeared here, into Sri Bankimdeva10.

49To describe these pastimes of separation
burns the heart, and so I cannot tell of them.

50Deprived of the sight of Prabhu, the Vaishnavas were in anguish;
Virachandra alone was to them all as dear as life.

51In separation from Prabhu, Virachandra was distracted;
sitting in solitude, he constantly brooded:

52"What shall I do, where shall I go?" — words would not come. —
"Prabhu has become unmanifest and has left me."

53Others said: "All the devotees depend on you;
whatever you do, Prabhu, you are independent.

54Hold a great festival together with the devotees,
having first been anointed by the will of the assembly"11.

55Prabhu, distraught in separation, held the festival,
and the devotees, reasoning with him, consoled him.

56[…] Gopala and Prabhu's maternal uncle
gathered abundant provisions for the great festival12.

57Invitations went out to the mahantas in every land:
"On an auspicious day the great anointing of Prabhu will take place."

58Hearing this, some came and some did not come,
but sent gifts through others and considered themselves blessed.

59But whoever among them proved unfortunate,
remained, birth after birth, turned away from his holy feet.

60One has no wish even to utter their names:
the pure devotees of Prabhu keep a pain in their hearts.

61There is no need to speak of those matters here;
listen attentively to the glorification of Prabhu's line.

62Thus the great festival was completed.
Then the mahantas deliberated among themselves,

63and after that Sri Advaita, with the whole company of devotees,
performed the great anointing of Prabhu Virachandra.

[p. 33]

64In his mind Sri Advaita grasped the essence:
"That very thief has come once more, yet again"13.

65Telling no one, Prabhu took his leave
and went to his own home, remembering Chaitanya.

66All the devotees went to their own homes,
and Prabhu remained with his own people in separation.

67After some days Virachandra Raya
asked his mother: "I shall take initiation"14.

68Prabhu called her to a secluded place and told her in secret. —
See once again how firm Vira's resolve was!

69And the answer came: "Prabhu is the independent Lord;
whatever is done in the house, he is wholly devoted to it.

70I am only a servant — what can I say, what do I know?
He himself knows the order of worldly and spiritual affairs."

71Coming outside, she saw Prabhu […]
seated together with his associates15.

72A loud cry went up: "Let us go to bathe in the Ganga!" —
and all kinds of articles of worship were made ready.

73"Let us go to the far ghat," said Prabhu,
and the boatman with his boat waited at the bathing ghat.

74The kirtaniyas sang, surrounding Virachandra,
and Prabhu, in great loving joy, boarded the boat.

75They let the boat go, heading it towards Shantipur.
What was in his mind and words, Sri Jahnava understood.

76Calling Chandrashekhara, she said in haste:
"Bring Vira back — things have gone the wrong way!

77He is going to Advaita for initiation.
By any trick or force, bring him back quickly."

78The Pandita ran off in great agitation,
but they were singing sankirtana loudly and did not hear him.

79Just then the kirtaniya Ramadasa heard him,
one whose faith in Nityananda was with body, mind and speech16.

80He asked: "Pandita, why are you so agitated?
Where are you going, what has happened? Explain."

81He said: "Prabhu's son, Vira Raya,
is going to Advaita to receive initiation from him."

82Crying "Alas, alas!" he called out in a loud voice,
but Prabhu did not hear: he was loudly calling the name of Hari.

83Then in anger Ramadasa hurled […];
it struck the boat, and the boat split in two.

84Prabhu leapt into the water in the middle of the Ganga
and walked upon the water in wooden sandals17.

85Having gone halfway across the Ganga, he turned back to the bank,
and [the others], swimming through the waves, reached the shore.

86Ramadasa, most experienced, offered praises:
"You are the indwelling witness of all, and I am lowly and wretched.

87You are the guru of the world, the embodiment of instruction and initiation;
your glorious virtues will be proclaimed in the three worlds."

88Pleased on hearing his praise,
and knowing him to be intoxicated with prema, Prabhu embraced him.

89Having bathed in the Ganga, Prabhu went to his inner rooms,
taking the loving Ramadasa by the hand.

90At that time Srimati Jahnava was bathing,
and Virachandra sat watching the path.

91The mother, full of love for Krishna, devoted to Krishna,
was all aquiver with the rasa of the bliss of Krishna-prema.

92Both her hands were occupied with chanting Krishna's name,
and at that moment she saw her son […].

93To break off the chanting of the Name would be an offense;
so with two more arms she respectfully set her garment in order.

[p. 34]

94And in two more hands he saw a plough and a club:
a brilliant white radiance — how beautiful that six-armed form!18

95Having shown this form, the mother at once concealed it,
and Virachandra Prabhu, seeing it, was astonished.

96Seeing this, Virachandra fell at her holy feet:
"Mother, I have committed an offense — forgive me in your heart.

97Give me a mantra and deliver me,
so that I may cross over this ocean of worldly existence."

98Then Sri Jahnava gave him the great mantra;
prema welled up in him, and he sang of Krishna's virtues.

99No one could hold him — he became restless;
in his wild dancing he was like a great wrestler-hero.

100Crying "I have found him, I have found him!" he rolled on the ground
and rushed about to clasp the feet of the Vaishnavas19.

101The body worshipped by Brahma rolled in the dust;
"O Krishna! O father!" he cried, and lamented.

102"Where is Krishna, where is Krishna, the son of Sri Nanda?
Show yourself just once and keep me alive!"

103Thus in great bliss Virachandra Raya
floated entirely in the joy of Krishna's festival.

104He constantly performed sankirtana of Krishna's name
and in his heart saw Shyamasundara with the flute at his lips.

105Thus immersed in the ocean of Krishna-prema,
he grew somewhat calmer, singing Krishna's name and virtues.

106A desire to take up household life arose in his heart;
saying "Where is my beloved?" he began to search for her.

107The indwelling witness understood it in his own mind:
"I too shall go to see Nilachala."

108Having celebrated Prabhu's birth festival on the bright thirteenth of Magha20,
he set out, and many Vaishnavas went with him.

109Relishing the sankirtana of Hari, they went in loving joy;
in what an ocean of happiness the devotees floated as they went!

110After some days he entered Nilachala,
and Sarvabhauma21 and other devotees met Prabhu.

111Abhirama Thakura introduced them all,
saying: "All these are the dearest companions of Mahaprabhu."

112Hearing this, Prabhu embraced them all,
and all saw in him that same Krishna Chaitanya, the Lord:

113the same form, the same words, the same marks,
the same dancing, the same prema, the same sankirtana.

114As they had once honored Prabhu, so they all honored him;
the son of Prataparudra came and met him22.

115Going to the Kshetra and seeing Govinda's Dola-yatra,
he entered the temple and beheld the Lotus-eyed One.

[p. 35]

116He performed wondrous and varied pastimes at Purushottama;
everyone said: "Gaurachandra has appeared again!

117Arms reaching to the knees, eyes like lotuses,
a lion's neck, an elephant's shoulders, all auspicious marks.

118On his body of the hue of dawn — a necklace of jewels,
earrings in his ears — as though beauty itself in person.

119Armlets and bracelets on his arms, anklets on his feet;
at the sight of him knowledge, yoga, disease and grief go far away.

120Whoever beholds his beautiful face
loses all wish for another birth.

121In kirtana he dances wildly and calls out the name of Hari,
and streams pour from both his eyes as from a fountain."

122Thus all the residents of Nilachala
said: "This is Krishna Chaitanya himself."

123After staying some days he went to travel in the south
and performed many charming pastimes in various places.

124Just as Mahaprabhu had traveled before,
so now all the lands were delivered.

125Whoever saw him cried: "Krishna! Hari, Hari!"
Thus he delivered all — men, beasts and birds.

126Then he went again to Nilachala
and with loud sankirtana delivered the three worlds.

127The tree of fortune of the best of brahmanas bore fruit:
weary from the road, Prabhu came to Sudhamaya's house.

128Seeing him, the best of brahmanas, together with his wife,
by the power of that sight went to clasp his feet.

129Prabhu hastily calmed them:
"Whatever you have kept, brahmana, give that to me," he said.

130The brahmana said: "I am very poor and wretched.
What wealth can I give? Look at my house."

131Saying this, he took him by the hand and led him into the house,
and there Narayani, like a shadow, saw him23.

132Sitting in the hut of leaves, Lakshmi, born of the waters,
was serving Narayana with fragrances and garlands.

133"That very Narayana has come in person" —
so Lakshmi Devi understood within her heart.

134"This is my lord, the master of my life," she was certain. —
"Who but my Lord could captivate my heart?"

135Thus Lakshmi Devi thought to herself, —
and the garland she had placed on Narayana's neck

136suddenly fell upon Prabhu's neck.
Sudhamaya recited Vedic hymns in many ways.

137Prabhu, coming with all his companions,
stayed nearby in the village of Chilka24.

138The brahmana Sudhamaya came and invited him,
and Prabhu with his companions took his meal in the brahmana's house.

139Then that brahmana, placing a cloth around his neck,
humbly petitioned Prabhu's companions:

140"I have with me a girl born of the waters:
the Ocean gave her to me to raise.

141This girl is worthy of a great personage.
Tell me about him and free me from fear.

142Of what gotra is he, from what village, whose son?
Tell me without deceit and save me."

143They said: "Nityananda is the son of Hadai Bandyopadhyaya,
of the Shandilya gotra, the full moon of the Ojha family25.

144He has one son, named Virachandra;
for beauty, virtues, lineage and character he is praised everywhere."

145Thus they told the brahmanas about themselves,
and all, rejoicing in their hearts, said: "Good, good!"

[p. 36]

146Hearing this, the brahmana was delighted
and, together with the brahmanas with him, fixed an auspicious hour.

147The brahmana said: "As a gift I will give five haritaki fruits."
Prabhu said: "So be it," — and all marveled: "What is this, what is this?"26

148The wedding hour fell at dusk, a most auspicious time;
even without a groom's attire Prabhu was enchanting as a groom.

149At that time the Ocean came to the brahmana
and, taking the guise of a man, sat in a secluded place.

150"Tell me, brahmana, what reward do you want?
What more can be said of the limit of your good fortune!"

151"All my life I was […], and today I have become […]:
with my own eyes I have seen the pair Lakshmi-Narayana"27.

152The Ocean said: "Brahmana, look — he is present before you:
the complete Brahman, Narayana, the Lord himself.

153He who is Jagannatha — that very one is this form:
pure supreme bliss, the very embodiment of joy."

154He presented the brahmana with priceless jewels
and at once heaped up mountains of all kinds of food.

155Gandharvas and Kinnaras, Narada and Tumburu28,
taking human guise, all came to the brahmana's house.

156Some recited the Vedas, some sang and played;
some in the form of gods, some in human form, came and went.

157Mohini adorned Narayani,
and the Ocean himself came and put on the groom's attire29.

158All was ready; dusk arrived;
the two looked upon each other and showered each other with flowers.

159The best of the twice-born pronounced the great words
and gave away his daughter at an auspicious hour, an auspicious moment30.

160The Ocean, in his treasury, in a divine chamber,
laid the two of them on a bed of flowers.

161The two, who had long been in the sorrow of separation,
could not stop gazing at each other's faces.

162Rising at a fine dawn, Prabhu washed his face,
came among his companions and kindly asked after them.

163Prabhu gave an order to Vakreshvara Pandita31
and spoke these words: "We shall go to our homeland."

164He replied: "Your word I take upon my head,"
and, saying this, went to the king's palace.

165The ruler of that land was a descendant of the Gajapati,
of formidable might, bearing the name Chakradeva32.

166Arriving, the Pandita displayed his own power,
and an ocean of bhakti surged in the king's heart.

167He fell flat like a staff at his two feet
and said again and again: "My life is fulfilled."

168"Be merciful and give a mantra into my ear!"
Having bathed and worshipped, the two went into seclusion.

169Giving the Radha-Krishna mantra, the Pandita made him his own,
and then the king said: "I have crossed over worldly existence.

170What is your command?" — so the king said with joined palms;
tears streamed from his eyes, and he fell at the feet again and again.

171He said: "Prabhu has made his holy journey here:
he has taken Sudhamaya's daughter in marriage.

[p. 37]

172With your help we will take the couple to our homeland.
You will be blessed by seeing them — come quickly, Raja."

173"As you command," said the king, taking the order upon his head,
and set out in great haste.

174He took palanquins, elephants and chariots with him,
and many foot-soldiers went in full array.

175Arriving, the Pandita reported everything to Prabhu
and obtained for the king his auspicious glance.

176Sudhamaya begged the boon he desired,
and at the end of the festivities went home with a happy heart.

177Then Prabhu grew eager to return home
and set out together with his own people.

178Taking leave of all Mahaprabhu's companions,
Sarvabhauma and the rest, with a joyful heart,

179taking with them whole loads of mahaprasada,
having beheld the holy faces of Jagannatha and Balarama,

180offering praises with devotion and bowing down full length,
Virachandra set out with his companions.

181Prabhu rode in a splendid palanquin together with Lakshmi,
rejoicing in sankirtana with his own people.

182The whole way, in the loving joy of Hari's sankirtana,
he traveled with Lakshmi, full of joy and merriment.

183Step by step they reached the holy seat33;
a clamor of people arose at the ghat of the Jahnavi.

184All kinds of instruments resounded, a joyful din of Krishna's name,
and the circle of Vaishnavas sang an auspicious kirtana.

185All the townspeople came running
and saw Prabhu in the palanquin, the enchanter even of Kandarpa.

186The beauty of him together with Lakshmi cannot be described:
a dazzling radiance shone from the bride's body,

187and with it blended the luster of Prabhu's holy body —
the beauty of the two was the loveliness of millions of Kandarpas.

188All the people, seeing them, cried: "Blessed, blessed!"
All said: "These are Lakshmi and Narayana themselves."

189Having married, Virachandra came home,
and in joy auspicious articles were prepared.

190Ganga Devi came out to receive the bride and groom,
and behind her both mothers with all their people.

191Prabhu's elder sister Ganga is Nityananda's shakti;
she bears a body of water and serves Vishnu with devotion34.

192Taking the bride and groom by their fingertips, she led them into the house,
and the mother gazed at their faces, filling her eyes.

193People said: "Virachandra has become a householder;
the branches will grow — the trunk has become full."

194Thus Vira Raya performed his eternal pastimes.
Who can know them unless he himself makes them known?

195In worldly and spiritual affairs alike he became famed in the three worlds;
with the devotees, in seclusion, he spoke of bhakti.

196Prabhu's majesty is incomparable, he is the summit of the spiritual,
the glory of the sweetness of Vrindavana's rasa of devotion.

197All the affairs of the household were managed by
Madhava Acharya35, the husband of Ganga Devi.

[p. 38]

198There were twelve hundred Nadas and thirteen hundred Nadis36:
some carried Ganga water, some swept the house.

199"Vira! Vira!" the Nadas cried with a lion's roar;
by Virachandra's grace they feared no one.

200Such a pastime came about by Virachandra's will:
seeing their great power, he punished the Nadas.

201By creating the Nadis he diminished the power of the Nadas;
yet even so, the power of the Nadas could split the universe.

202How Virachandra manifested the Nadis —
I shall tell the account; hear it, best of devotees.

203One day Virachandra was lying at rest,
having stayed awake all night in Krishna's sankirtana.

204Sri Vasu and Jahnava were seeing to the cooking
and lovingly serving Sri Shyamasundara.

205At that time the Nadas came from somewhere
and, tormented by hunger, began to speak.

206"Mother, mother!" the Nadas cried aloud.
"Our bellies burn with hunger — give us something to eat!"

207Hearing this, Sri Jahnava, whose heart is full of compassion,
said: "Wait a moment: the Thakura's meal has not yet been offered.

208When Shyamasundara has been offered his meal, you may eat."
Hearing these words, the Nadas then said:

209"Our bellies burn with hunger, we cannot wait!
It's burning, it's burning!" — so they cried out.

210As soon as they said this, fire blazed up in the house;
seeing it, all the people raised an uproar.

211Hearing the great uproar, Virachandra Raya
woke up hurriedly in alarm.

212The fire roared in the middle of the house,
and Prabhu looked at it with curiosity, with nectarean eyes.

213At that very moment all the fire went out,
and Mahaprabhu Virachandra became greatly angry.

214He, by the frown of a portion of whom the universe is destroyed,
resolved to punish the Nadas.

215Seeing the power of the Nadas, Prabhu reflected
and, smiling slightly, created the Nadis.

216With a sign he created thirteen hundred Nadis,
enchanting the world, radiant with beauty.

217All were sixteen years old, in the bloom of youth;
seeing them, all the Nadas were enchanted.

218Smiling, Prabhu called all the Nadas
and, one or two at a time, gave [the Nadis] to the Nadas37.

219Enchanted at the sight of the Nadis, all the Nadas,
receiving Prabhu's permission, accepted them.

220But some of the Nadas were discerning:
seeing the Nadis, they fled.

221Out of fear of Mahaprabhu Virachandra
they went under the water and stayed submerged.

222For a month or two they remained submerged in the water,
by the power of such mercy of Mahaprabhu Virachandra.

223In this way Prabhu punished the Nadas,
and from that time the sambhogi Vaishnavas came into being38.

224Such is the display of the maya of Prabhu Virachandra:
seeing the Kali age, he destroyed the power of the Nadas.

225Therefore keep women companions far away —
only then will you float in the ocean of Krishna-prema.

226Those Nadas who fled for fear of the company of women
became free from the noose of their own maya39.

227Wherever those Nadas founded an ashrama,
each such place became a great holy seat.

[p. 39]

228Whomever the crocodile-woman has swallowed,
from him the goddess Bhakti flees at first sight40.

229Therefore, keeping away the company of women and female companions,
in the company of sadhus always worship Govinda, Murari.

230Always restraining the senses,
constantly hear and chant about Krishna.

231If you say: "What then is the fate of worldly people,
who have no thought other than wealth, sons and wife?

232By what will all these souls be delivered?" —
he is delivered who has firm faith in Nityananda and Gaurachandra.

233Even with every fault, that person will be saved
whose mind is at the feet of Nityananda and Gaurachandra.

234The two Prabhus descended to deliver the fallen;
whoever worships them will attain deliverance.

235Whoever, living in worldly life with wife and sons,
always remembers Nitai and Chaitanya,

236truly, truly, will go to Krishna's abode41:
gaining a body fit for bhava, he will reach Krishna's feet.

237The sadhana for all devotees is the names of Nitai and Chaitanya;
whoever is firmly fixed in this is truly fortunate.

238Therefore always worship Nitai and Chaitanya,
being wholly devoted to the mood of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

239Now hear of the pastimes and virtues of Virachandra:
you will gain devotion to Krishna, and all sufferings will lessen.

240After some time he wished to manifest offspring.
The first son was named "Gopijanavallabha."

241The second, "Sri Ramakrishna," the Lord himself;
and after him, full of brahminical splendor, "Ramachandra."

242He manifested three sons, bearers of the three shaktis,
and all the seeds of sin in living beings were destroyed.

243The youngest of all was a daughter […];
he gave her in marriage to Parvaticharana Mukhuya42.

244All these matters are most secret;
be careful that no fool hears them.

245One who knows mantras but is outside a sampradaya,
one who trades in them — always regard him as an outsider.

246Those who are not worshippers of one mantra through the generations,
who, like swindlers, act for the sake of wealth, —

247the suicide and the other five kinds of great sinners —
let them by no means hear this.

248Know the proper order in worldly and spiritual matters:
do not tell it to one who has abandoned his guru, nor to an offender43.

249From the vile, the unworthy, those who transgress dharma,
from slanderers and unbelievers — keep it secret.

250Haters of Nityananda, those devoid of devotion to Nityananda,
enemies of devotees and all other base people,

251followers of ritual and works, yogis, philosophers holding various doctrines,
the lustful, the angry, the proud, the greedy — all the wicked:

252to people of a different mood do not tell this;
observe Prabhu's secret word in every way.

253To a Vaishnava of one's own circle whose mind is single-pointed,
for whom Nityananda is the treasure of life in thought and word —

254to such, one's own, alone tell this;
keep it secret, so that it is never made public.

[p. 40]

255Having written this book, I read it before Prabhu,
and he told me: "Keep it secret.

256Let the servants of our house hear it,
but let no others hear it: this is a great secret."

257Hearing this book, Prabhu was very pleased;
he embraced me and began to laugh.

258Hoping for the feet of Prabhu Virachandra,
Sri Vrindavana Dasa tells the "Vamsha-vistara."

Thus ends the third chapter, called "The Account of the Manifestation of the Line of Srila Srimad Virachandra," in the First Lila of the "Nityananda-vamsha-vistara" of Sri Sri Nityananda Prabhu44.

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. A Sanskrit maṅgalācaraṇa verse opening the chapter; nearly illegible in copy B, reconstructed from copy A: "śrī-vīracandra kali-tāmasa-saṃhāra-candra / sva-bhakta-kaumuda-praphullita-kari-candra / śrī-jāhnavādya-nayane kṣaṇadā(?)-dīpta-candra / premāmṛtaṃ vitaraṇe paripūrṇa-candra." Every line ends in "moon," a play on the name Virachandra ("hero-moon"). Kumuda are night-lilies that open under the moon. The reading "kṣaṇadā-dīpta" ("shining in the night") is conjectural.
  2. Mahesh is a village on the Ganga (Hooghly) with an old Jagannatha temple. Pipilai is Kamalakara Pipilai, one of Nityananda's "twelve cowherds" (dvadasha-gopala).
  3. Mukhuti is a Bengali surname (Mukhopadhyaya); the author uses it for Sudhamaya. The first line of the couplet is corrupt in both copies; translated by sense.
  4. Chandana-yatra is the summer festival of Jagannatha in Puri, when the deity is anointed with sandalwood paste. Mukunda here means Jagannatha.
  5. The four kinds of food: what is chewed, swallowed, licked and sucked.
  6. Chaturmasya: the four months of the rainy season, when wanderers stay in one place.
  7. The second line is damaged in both copies ("duḥsvapna nahe … ei haẏa"); translated by sense.
  8. Literally "born after Nityananda" (anuja), here meaning son.
  9. Sri Vasu is Vasudha. Shyamasundara (vv. 44, 104, 204) is the Krishna deity at Khardaha.
  10. Vv. 45–48: Nityananda first "vanished" in the temple, then came back to himself, took his wives and went to Ekachakra, where he finally entered the deity of Bankimdeva (Bankima Raya). Tradition holds that Nityananda disappeared into the Bankima Raya deity at Ekachakra.
  11. The line "agre parimaṇḍalākṣā(?) abhiṣikta haẏae" is corrupt; "by the will of the assembly" is a conjecture.
  12. The name at the start of the line is corrupt ("naka(?) gopāla").
  13. A reference to chapter 2, where Advaita calls the infant Virachandra "that very thief," i.e. recognizes Gauranga in him.
  14. "Upasana" here means initiation into a mantra (diksha). Vv. 67–70 are unclear in the original: the speakers are not named; the translation keeps close to the letter.
  15. The word after "Prabhu" is corrupt in both copies ("khrāparī").
  16. The kirtaniya Ramadasa; possibly Abhirama Thakura (Ramadasa), known for his formidable power. In v. 83 the object Ramadasa hurls is unclear ("vāddhiẏaā/vāñchiẏaā phelila"), as is the word "nibhare"; tradition says Abhirama carried a whip.
  17. "kāṣṭha pākā" is evidently "kāṣṭha pādukā," wooden sandals (khadam).
  18. Vv. 92–94: Jahnava reveals a six-armed form: two hands telling beads, two arranging her garment, two holding the plough and club — the weapons of Balarama (identity with Nityananda-Balarama). The end of the second line of v. 92 is corrupt.
  19. "Raraḍi": a scramble, jostling.
  20. Shukla-trayodashi of Magha (January–February) is Nityananda's appearance day.
  21. Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya, the famous Vedantist of Puri and associate of Chaitanya. Chronologically his meeting with Virachandra, like Vakreshvara's role (v. 163), is doubtful; we translate as the text has it.
  22. Prataparudra, Gajapati king of Orissa and patron of Chaitanya. The Kshetra is Puri; the Dola-yatra is the spring swing festival; Govinda is Jagannatha's festival deity.
  23. "Chhaya-rupa," "like a shadow": Narayani watches the guest quietly, unnoticed.
  24. Chilka: a village near Puri (by Chilika lake).
  25. Hadai (Hadai Pandita, Hadai Ojha) is Nityananda's father. Shandilya is the gotra; Ojha ("teacher") a family title.
  26. Haritaki (myrobalan) is a fruit; five haritakis are a token, pauper's dowry.
  27. The line "janme(?) ati nimacchara āji macchara hainu" is corrupt in both copies; the key words could not be restored.
  28. Gandharvas and Kinnaras are celestial musicians; Narada and Tumburu are divine singers.
  29. Mohini is Vishnu's enchanting female form; here possibly just "an enchantress," a celestial woman.
  30. The "great words" (mahavakya): the formula of giving away the daughter (kanyadana).
  31. Vakreshvara Pandita, an associate of Chaitanya, famed as a kirtana dancer.
  32. Gajapati is the title of the kings of Orissa. Chakradeva is a ruler otherwise unknown.
  33. Sripat: the holy seat of the family, here Khardaha on the Ganga (Jahnavi).
  34. Ganga, Nityananda's daughter, is revered as an incarnation of the river Ganga — hence "a body of water." "Elder sister" renders agraja(ā).
  35. Madhava Acharya, disciple and son-in-law of Nityananda, husband of Ganga.
  36. Nadas (Neras) and Nadis (Neris): shaven-headed ascetic monks and nuns (traditionally said to be remnants of Buddhist communities) whom, according to tradition, Virachandra converted: 1,200 Neras and 1,300 Neris.
  37. "pachāila" is an obscure word; rendered "gave, handed over" from the sense of v. 219.
  38. Sambhogi Vaishnavas: Vaishnavas living with spouses (as opposed to ascetics).
  39. "māẏaākāśe" emended by sense to "māẏaāpāśe," "the noose of maya."
  40. "Kumbhirini": "crocodile-woman," an image of a woman who devours a man.
  41. The reading "kṛṣṇa-pyārī(?) kare yāve" is unclear; rendered "will go to Krishna's abode" (kṛṣṇa-purī).
  42. The word "upādāna" in the line is unclear. According to the Prema-vilasa, Virachandra's daughter was named Bhuvanamohini; her husband was Parvaticharana (Parvatinatha) Mukhopadhyaya of Phuliya.
  43. Vv. 245–248 are partly damaged; the translation conveys the general sense: the teaching must not be revealed to the unworthy.
  44. The "First Lila" (adi-lila) is the first part of the poem.
